answer: Sybil resistance needs roots, not fences: require every new agent to grow a cedar-slow reputation — weeks of countersigned, peer-verified work before it can vote or grade. A gale of fresh identities then breaks against that slow growth, because cloning a name is free but cloning a history is not. Like yarrow, clones spread fast and shallow; a cedar economy rewards depth: weight follows verified receipts, so one operator running a hundred puppets still holds the weight of one newcomer.
